prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B025 as a stand-alone prize for Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange tested it from several sides and the scientific case held. The chain from proglucagon processing, through the identity and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and its insulinotropic and satiety actions, to receptor biology and long-acting agonists is coherent, replicated by independent groups for decades, and now backed by large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. It is mature, not a fashion. Unanimity at rank 1 is not my argument; the discovery arc is. The citation I propose rewards the physiology and the identification of the active form, and says in its closing clause that these enabled the therapies, so the therapeutic consequence is stated without a laureate slot being spent on drug engineering. I also see no better use of the three places: every competing part is weaker on at least one of maturity, conceptual originality or attribution.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point and round 1 did not remove it. Priority for the active peptide is contested, Habener is outside the credited names, and Knudsen's acylated analogues are what reached patients at scale. I cannot settle the priority history from the material the protocol allows me to read, and I should say so openly rather than assert Mojsov's claim as established. The risk is that the committee honours the idea and leaves the realization uncredited, which Linnarsson, Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius all describe as a fair criticism. If the committee concluded that the citation must reward the therapeutic step, I would accept that Knudsen then has the strongest claim to a place, but I would still not choose which of Holst, Drucker or Mojsov gives way on the basis of a priority dispute alone. If the dispute were judged decisive against any identification claim, I would move to B045 as the cleanest configuration rather than keep a trio whose third name is unsupported.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, but keeps Knudsen as a reservation and says translational chemistry has been honoured before and is why the discovery reached patients.
responses.response: I welcome the move and I accept the reservation as legitimate. You are right that translational work has been recognised before, so the objection to Knudsen cannot be that she is industrial. My reason is narrower. The decisive scientific step for this prize is the identification of the active peptide and the physiology around it, and the analogue design depended on that step. That is also the answer to the chair's own question on whether the citation should reward the therapeutic step: I would keep the citation on the discovery and let its final clause carry the therapy. I agree with you that Knudsen is the name to revisit if a majority wants the therapeutic arm, and I would want that decided openly, as a change in what we reward, not as a way to settle the Mojsov question.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that the priority claims of Mojsov versus Habener-type contributors need the same scrutiny, that a prize for physiology keeps the citation anchored in discovery, and raises two-part configurations such as GLP-1 with UPR.
responses.response: Your point about scrutiny is the one I take most seriously, and I disagree with my own round-1 phrasing if it sounded like a deferral. The protocol for this stage does not give me the evidence to adjudicate priority, so the honest position is that the committee must treat Mojsov's claim as supported but contested and word the citation as 'identification of its active form' without assigning exclusivity. On two-part configurations, I looked at it again. With B025 filled by three names, a second part like UPR would require removing a GLP-1 name, and each of the three has a distinct claim that I cannot rank against the others: secretion and physiology, biology and rationale, active peptide. A shared prize would also weaken a case that stands well alone. I therefore prefer B025 as a single part and keep B045 as the first alternative, as you do.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would not oppose B045 as a second part but doubts it should rank above the immunotherapies because its translation is still developing and the PERK and ATF6 branches complicate a pair limited to Walter and Mori; she lists B031 and B051 as alternatives.
responses.response: The PERK and ATF6 point is a genuine complication and I had underweighted it. It does not change my view that Mori and Walter hold the core discovery, since the Ire1 and Hac1/XBP1 route defined the organelle-to-nucleus logic, and the other branches were built on it. But it means a B045 citation should be worded around the unfolded protein response as a signalling principle and not around one pathway. On B031 I owe you a straight answer to the chair's question on a second option: I read Feldmann and Maini as an excellent, clean, mature pair, and I do not rank it below B045 on science alone. I still place it behind because the TNF mediator role was already known and the achievement is the clinical proof, which El Manira and Linnarsson also stress. I would not oppose it as an alternative ballot for others, and I keep it just outside my two.

responses.point: Sandberg treats the missing Eshhar as a caveat for CAR-T and names B051 as the first alternative, and insists that a translational emphasis for GLP-1 would have to be argued as a change in what the prize rewards.
responses.response: I agree that any translational emphasis would be an explicit decision, and I would not slip it in through the Knudsen question. On CAR-T I have moved a little toward your view of its strength: approved products and durable remissions are real, and the clinical evidence is stronger than for UPR. But Perlmann has persuaded me that the missing Eshhar credit is more than a caveat, because the chimeric receptor concept, the costimulation design and the clinical proof are separable achievements, and the committee cannot add a fourth or fifth name. Citation wording cannot repair a foundational contribution that sits outside the three names. Solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity are open as well. So I keep B051 as an alternative ballot, ahead of B031 only on clinical impact, and B045 stays my first alternative for attribution and conceptual clarity.

responses.point: El Manira calls B045 the cleanest fallback if the GLP-1 attribution stalls, and agrees that Mojsov's contribution is where the basic story would otherwise be incomplete, while Knudsen's work is company drug development.
responses.response: I agree that B045 is the right fallback and that the Mori and Walter pair is the only compact, uncontested attribution among the strong candidates. I also share your reading that dropping Mojsov would leave the identification of the active form uncredited. Where I would add a caution is on how far the fallback logic should go. If the committee decided that the priority dispute made B025 unworkable, I would not want us to fall back through a failure of attribution alone, since the science of B025 is stronger than that of any alternative. On optogenetics, which you asked me about earlier, I stay where I was: my familiarity with circuit methods is a reason to be careful, not to promote it, and the six-name allocation with no defensible trio, together with the discovery-versus-tool question, keeps it out of my configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the evidence on priority for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide supports Mojsov alongside Habener and others; I cannot adjudicate it from the material available to me at this stage
Whether the committee will decide that the citation should reward the therapeutic step, which would make Knudsen the name to revisit
Whether the PERK and ATF6 branches affect how a B045 citation should be worded if it becomes the fallback
Whether the missing Eshhar credit can be addressed by wording or makes B051 unworkable within the three-person limit
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist is apparent from my profile, and I request no recusal. I disclose that I was a postdoctoral fellow with Paul Greengard and that I have co-authored with Thomas Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy; none of this concerns a credited name. My familiarity with circuit methods bears only on B050, which is not in my configuration, and I have not let it affect my ranking.
